11	
12	# Spacetime Canvas — Implementation Plan
13	
14	**Feature family:** Temporal Observatory
15	**This document:** the build plan for the **Spacetime Canvas** — the first and
16	load-bearing surface of the family.
17	**Ticket:** T-047 (Foundation) → this plan expands it.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 0. Why "Spacetime Canvas"
22	
23	The platform already has a **Research Canvas**: a surface where the user
24	arranges *ideas* — entities, relationships, notes — in conceptual space.
25	
26	The **Spacetime Canvas** is its sibling: the same verb, a different axis. The
27	user arranges and traverses *evidence in space and time*. Same posture
28	(a canvas you work on, not a chart you look at), same design grammar,
29	orthogonal dimension.
30	
31	This naming is deliberate and load-bearing. Keep the pairing visible in
32	routes, module names, and copy:
33	
34	| Surface | Organizes | Route | Module |
35	|---|---|---|---|
36	| Research Canvas | ideas, entities, relations | `/research-canvas` | `features/mindmap/` |
37	| Spacetime Canvas | evidence across space + time | `/spacetime` | `features/spacetime/` |
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 1. The architectural finding (load-bearing)
42	
43	The reference scroll UI — `v0-ultraterrestrial-research-canva.vercel.app/timeline-explorer`
44	— was inspected live on 2026-08-01. What it actually is:
45	
46	```
47	Next.js  +  GSAP  +  Lenis (smooth scroll)
48	22,056px scroll height  ≈  24 viewport-heights,  19 encounters
49	ZERO <canvas> elements.  No Three.js, no R3F, no WebGL.
50	```
51	
52	Its DOM has exactly two structural layers:
53	
54	```
55	.fixed.inset-0.overflow-hidden.bg-neutral-950     ← BACKGROUND: a stack of 8
56	   ├── img roswell-ufo-crash-site-desert.jpg         cross-fading <img> era
57	   ├── img washington-dc-capitol-ufo-1952.jpg        plates, pinned to viewport
58	   ├── img socorro-new-mexico-ufo-egg-shaped…
59	   └── …
60	
61	.absolute.inset-0                                  ← NARRATIVE: CSS 3D
62	   perspective: 900px                                 cards fly toward the
63	   transform-style: preserve-3d                       viewer on scroll
64	   └── matrix3d(…, translateZ(-674px), …)
65	```
66	
67	**The seam:** the background is a *slot*, currently filled with static images,
68	and the narrative layer above it never touches WebGL. So:
69	
70	> **The Spacetime Canvas globe drops into the `.fixed.inset-0` slot, and the
71	> scroll narrative becomes Guided Investigations rendered as descent.**
72	
73	This unifies three storyboarded concepts into one surface instead of three:
74	
75	- **Concept 01 (Spacetime Canvas)** → the fixed globe layer
76	- **Concept 02 (Guided Investigation)** → the scrolling waypoint cards
77	- The **adaptive temporal dial** → the left rail, already present as a year ladder
78	
79	Scroll position becomes the single driver: `scrollProgress → temporalCursor →
80	{ globe camera, active layers, visible waypoint }`.
81	
82	### Why this is worth doing rather than building two surfaces
83	
84	The alternative — a globe page and a separate scroll page — reproduces exactly
85	the failure ADR 0002 rejected for GL4SS: two navigation systems, two state
86	models, a jarring seam between "exploring" and "reading." One surface with a
87	live background is the whole point.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 2. Three risks to verify *while* building
92	
93	These are not blockers; they are measurements to take at the point they become
94	answerable. Do not hand-wave any of them.
95	
96	### R1 — `position: fixed` WebGL under a `preserve-3d` sibling
97	
98	An `<img>` stack is nearly free to keep pinned. A live deck.gl globe re-renders
99	every frame *while* Lenis drives `matrix3d` transforms on the sibling layer.
100	Compositing a `preserve-3d` subtree over a continuously-repainting WebGL canvas
101	is a known source of jank even when each half is 60fps alone.
102	
103	Current weight, from the 2026-08-01 production build:
104	
105	| Route | Route JS | First load |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `/research-canvas` | 500 kB | 1.23 MB |
108	| `/timeline` | 195 kB | 737 kB |
109	| `/sightings` | 38.4 kB | 398 kB |
110	
111	**Verify by measuring, not reasoning.** Spike task: mount the existing
112	sightings globe inside a `perspective`/`preserve-3d` scroll container and
113	record frame timing before building anything on top. If it janks, the fallback
114	is a **static globe plate per waypoint** (render-to-texture / prerendered
115	frames) with the live globe reserved for the free-exploration mode.
116	
117	### R2 — Is the temporal cursor driven, or driving?
118	
119	Concept 01 shows the user **scrubbing** the adaptive dial. The scroll UI has
120	**scroll** driving position. These are opposite directions of control.
121	
122	If scroll is the only input, the dial degrades to a readout and
123	`TemporalCursor` collapses to its `station` variant — the `exact` and `range`
124	modes in `TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md` §3.3 become dead types.
125	
126	**Decision required before `spacetime-store.ts` is written.** Getting this
127	wrong is a rewrite, not a tweak.
128	
129	**Recommendation — bidirectional, cursor is source of truth:**
130	
131	```
132	temporalCursor  ← THE single source of truth
133	   ↑ scroll (guided mode: scroll writes cursor, camera follows)
134	   ↑ dial    (free mode: dial writes cursor, scroll position follows)
135	```
136	
137	Scroll and dial are two *inputs* to one cursor, never two cursors. A `mode`
138	flag (`'guided' | 'free'`) decides which input is authoritative at a given
139	moment, so they can never fight.
140	
141	### R3 — 19 hardcoded cases ≠ a query layer
142	
143	The reference page is a fixed narrative over static images. The spec's §8 API
144	is viewport + time-window bounded. These are different work.
145	
146	Good news, from the subagent's audit: `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings` **already**
147	does year-range querying, `limit`, and 10-year batching via
148	`getSightingsByTimeChunk`. `sightings-globe.tsx:22` simply bypasses it and
149	loads a static `/sightings.geojson`.
150	
151	So Foundation is mostly **wiring an existing bounded API to the globe**, not
152	building one. But it does *not* make the scroll narrative data-driven — that is
153	separate, later work.
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 3. The reconstruction lever (non-negotiable)
158	
159	`TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md` §9 requires that generation happen only through an
160	unmistakable deliberate action. Concept 01 frame 4 shows a reconstruction
161	preview inline in the browse flow. **The lever wins.**
162	
163	In a scroll-driven UI this matters *more*, not less: **scrolling past a
164	waypoint is not an intent signal.** Auto-generating on scroll is precisely the
165	failure GL4SS redesigned itself around after pausing on a timeline became a
166	billable event.
167	
168	Rules:
169	
170	1. Scroll **never** triggers generation.
171	2. Reconstructions already in the archive may render freely on scroll — they
172	   cost nothing.
173	3. Generating a *new* reconstruction requires an explicit click on a control
174	   that names the cost.
175	4. The control is visually distinct from every navigation affordance on the
176	   surface.
177	
178	---
179

181	
182	### M0 — Foundation (this milestone)
183	
184	Goal: **one surface, one state model, one temporal cursor, live data.**
185	
186	| # | Task | Files | Risk |

189	| M0.2 | `spacetime.ts` types — `TemporalCursor`, `SpacetimeEvent`, `TemporalLayerFeature` | `features/spacetime/types/` | R2 |
190	| M0.3 | `spacetime-store.ts` — Zustand slice, cursor as single source of truth, `mode: guided \| free` | `features/spacetime/state/` | R2 |
191	| M0.4 | `temporal-stations.ts` — station ladder from event density | `features/spacetime/lib/` | — |
192	| M0.5 | Wire `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings` (already bounded) to the globe; delete the static `sightings.geojson` path | `features/sightings/sightings-globe.tsx:22` | R3 |

196	
197	**M0 exit criteria:** open `/spacetime`, scroll, watch the globe camera and the

199	and credibility. No reconstruction, no compare, no playback.
200	
201	### M1 — Evidence instrument
202	Layer panel · credibility + provenance filtering · event inspector ·
203	relationship arcs · precision/uncertainty rendering.
204	
205	### M2 — Reconstruction
206	Event Evidence Packet · staged scene planning · one still-image mode ·
207	central artifact + manifest storage · the lever · synthetic labeling.
208	
209	### M3 — Comparative analysis
210	Pinned comparison · seam / blink / onion / difference · evidence deltas.
211	(Concept 03)
212	
213	### M4 — Narrative
214	Guided Investigations · waypoint choreography · flap playback ·
215	space-time capsules. (Concepts 02, 04)
216	
217	**Do not start M2–M4 work during M0.** They are storyboarded, which makes them
218	tempting; they are phases 3–5 in the spec's own sequence.
219

12	
13	function eventsToGeoJSON(events: SpacetimeEvent[]): GeoJSON.FeatureCollection {
14	  return {
15	    type: 'FeatureCollection',
16	    features: events
17	      .filter((e) => e.coordinates)
18	      .map((e) => ({
19	        type: 'Feature' as const,
20	        geometry: {
21	          type: 'Point' as const,
22	          coordinates: [e.coordinates!.longitude, e.coordinates!.latitude],
23	        },
24	        properties: {
25	          id: e.id,
26	          title: e.title,
27	          timestamp: e.timestamp,
28	          credibility: e.credibilityScore ?? 0.5,
29	          epistemic: e.epistemicStatus ?? 'inferred',
30	        },
31	      })),
32	  }
33	}
34	
35	/**
36	 * Live Mapbox background for the Spacetime Canvas.

46	  const selectEvent = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.selectEvent)
47	  const setViewport = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setViewport)
48	
49	  const visibleEvents = useMemo(
50	    () => filterSpacetimeEvents(events, layers, filters),
51	    [events, layers, filters],
52	  )
53	  const geojson = useMemo(() => eventsToGeoJSON(visibleEvents), [visibleEvents])
54	
55	  // Boot map once
56	  useEffect(() => {
57	    const token = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_PUBLIC_TOKEN
58	    if (!token || !containerRef.current || mapRef.current) return
59	
60	    mapboxgl.accessToken = token

66	      attributionControl: false,
67	      pitch: 0,
68	    })
69	
70	    map.on('load', () => {
71	      map.addSource(SOURCE_ID, {type: 'geojson', data: geojson})

73	        id: LAYER_ID,

76	        paint: {

80	            ['get', 'credibility'],

82	            3,
83	            0.85,
84	            7,

86	          'circle-color': [
87	            'match',
88	            ['get', 'epistemic'],
89	            'documented',
90	            '#86efac',
91	            'disputed',
92	            '#fda4af',

94	          ],

96	          'circle-stroke-width': 1,
97	          'circle-stroke-color': '#0a0a0a',
98	        },
99	      })
100	    })
101	
102	    map.on('click', LAYER_ID, (e) => {
103	      const id = e.features?.[0]?.properties?.id
104	      if (typeof id === 'string') selectEvent(id)
105	    })
106

152	      .map((e) => ({

154	        dt: Math.abs(new Date(e.timestamp).getTime() - ts),

156	      .sort((a, b) => a.dt - b.dt)
157	      .slice(0, 12)

159	    if (nearby.length === 0) return

161	    const avgLng =
162	      nearby.reduce((s, n) => s + n.e.coordinates!.longitude, 0) / nearby.length
163	    const avgLat =
164	      nearby.reduce((s, n) => s + n.e.coordinates!.latitude, 0) / nearby.length
165	
166	    map.easeTo({
167	      center: [avgLng, avgLat],
168	      duration: 900,
169	      essential: true,
170	    })
171	  }, [cursor, visibleEvents])

1	'use server'
2	
3	import {getSightingsByTimeChunk} from '@/services/sightings/get-sightings'
4	import {sightingsToSpacetimeEvents} from '../lib/normalize'
5	import {buildTemporalStations} from '../lib/temporal-stations'
6	import type {SpacetimeEvent, TemporalStation} from '../types/spacetime'
7	
8	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsInput {
9	  startYear?: number
10	  endYear?: number
11	  limit?: number
12	}
13	
14	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsResult {
15	  events: SpacetimeEvent[]
16	  stations: TemporalStation[]
17	  timeRange: {startYear: number; endYear: number}
18	  /** Events that have coordinates — what the globe can render */
19	  geolocatedCount: number
20	}
21	
22	const DECADE_SPAN = 10
23	
24	/**
25	 * M0.5 data path: bounded Postgres query → SpacetimeEvent[] + stations.
26	 *
27	 * Uses the existing `getSightingsByTimeChunk` service (same substrate as
28	 * `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings`) via a server action so the canvas does
29	 * not need the INTERNAL_API_KEY header the REST route requires.
30	 *
31	 * Wide ranges are sampled per decade so `ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n`
32	 * cannot collapse the canvas into only the most recent years.
33	 *
34	 * Does NOT load static `/sightings.geojson`.
35	 */
36	export async function loadSpacetimeEvents(
37	  input: LoadSpacetimeEventsInput = {},
38	): Promise<LoadSpacetimeEventsResult> {
39	  const startYear = input.startYear ?? 1940
40	  const endYear = input.endYear ?? new Date().getUTCFullYear()
41	  // Keep first paint bounded; later milestones page by viewport + cursor.
42	  const limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? 400, 800)
43	
44	  const sightings = await fetchStratifiedSightings(startYear, endYear, limit)
45	  const events = sightingsToSpacetimeEvents(sightings).sort(
46	    (a, b) => new Date(a.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(b.timestamp).getTime(),
47	  )
48	  const stations = buildTemporalStations(events, {
49	    historicalStartYear: startYear,
50	    historicalEndYear: endYear,
51	  })
52	
53	  return {
54	    events,
55	    stations,
56	    timeRange: {startYear, endYear},
57	    geolocatedCount: events.filter((e) => e.coordinates).length,
58	  }
59	}
60	
61	async function fetchStratifiedSightings(
62	  startYear: number,
63	  endYear: number,
64	  limit: number,
65	) {
66	  const span = Math.max(1, endYear - startYear + 1)
67	
68	  // Narrow windows: one query is fine.
69	  if (span <= DECADE_SPAN) {
70	    return getSightingsByTimeChunk(startYear, endYear, limit)
71	  }
72	
73	  const decades: Array<{from: number; to: number}> = []
74	  const startDecade = Math.floor(startYear / DECADE_SPAN) * DECADE_SPAN
75	  for (let year = startDecade; year <= endYear; year += DECADE_SPAN) {
76	    const from = Math.max(startYear, year)
77	    const to = Math.min(endYear, year + DECADE_SPAN - 1)
78	    if (from <= to) decades.push({from, to})
79	  }
80	
81	  const perDecade = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(limit / decades.length))
82	  const batches = await Promise.all(
83	    decades.map(({from, to}) => getSightingsByTimeChunk(from, to, perDecade)),
84	  )
85	
86	  const byId = new Map<string, (typeof batches)[number][number]>()
87	  for (const batch of batches) {
88	    for (const sighting of batch) {
89	      byId.set(sighting.id, sighting)
90	    }
91	  }
92	
93	  return [...byId.values()]
94	    .sort((a, b) => a.timestamp.getTime() - b.timestamp.getTime())
95	    .slice(0, limit)
96	}
97

164	    raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick)
165	    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf)
166	  }, [setLastFrameMs])
167	}
168	
169	function useScrollProgressBridge() {
170	  const setScrollProgress = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setScrollProgress)
171	  const setTemporalCursor = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setTemporalCursor)
172	
173	  useEffect(() => {
174	    const narrative = document.querySelector('[data-spacetime-layer="narrative"]')
175	    if (!(narrative instanceof HTMLElement)) return
176	
177	    const onScroll = () => {
178	      const max = narrative.scrollHeight - narrative.clientHeight
179	      const progress = max > 0 ? narrative.scrollTop / max : 0
180	      setScrollProgress(progress)
181	
182	      // guided mode: scroll writes cursor (station approximation from sample waypoints)
183	      const idx = Math.min(
184	        SAMPLE_WAYPOINTS.length - 1,
185	        Math.floor(progress * SAMPLE_WAYPOINTS.length),
186	      )
187	      const wp = SAMPLE_WAYPOINTS[idx]
188	      if (!wp) return
189	      setTemporalCursor({
190	        mode: 'station',
191	        stationId: `spike-${wp.year}`,
192	        timestamp: `${wp.year}-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`,
193	      })
194	    }
195	
196	    narrative.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, {passive: true})
197	    onScroll()
198	    return () => narrative.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll)
199	  }, [setScrollProgress, setTemporalCursor])
200	}
201	
202	export function Preserve3dGlobeSpike() {
203	  useFrameTiming()
204	  useScrollProgressBridge()
205	
206	  return (
207	    <SpacetimeCanvasShell
208	      background={<SpikeBackgroundMap />}
209	      narrative={<SpikeNarrative />}
210	      chrome={<SpikeChrome />}
211	    />
212	  )
213	}
214

## Details on call tree & network request formats:
Information on performance traces may contain main thread activity represented as call frames and network requests.

Each call frame is presented in the following format:

'id;eventKey;name;duration;selfTime;urlIndex;childRange;[line];[column];[S]'

Key definitions:

* id: A unique numerical identifier for the call frame. Never mention this id in the output to the user.
* eventKey: String that uniquely identifies this event in the flame chart.
* name: A concise string describing the call frame (e.g., 'Evaluate Script', 'render', 'fetchData').
* duration: The total execution time of the call frame, including its children.
* selfTime: The time spent directly within the call frame, excluding its children's execution.
* urlIndex: Index referencing the "All URLs" list. Empty if no specific script URL is associated.
* childRange: Specifies the direct children of this node using their IDs. If empty ('' or 'S' at the end), the node has no children. If a single number (e.g., '4'), the node has one child with that ID. If in the format 'firstId-lastId' (e.g., '4-5'), it indicates a consecutive range of child IDs from 'firstId' to 'lastId', inclusive.
* line: An optional field for a call frame's line number. This is where the function is defined.
* column: An optional field for a call frame's column number. This is where the function is defined.
* S: _Optional_. The letter 'S' terminates the line if that call frame was selected by the user.

Example Call Tree:

1;r-123;main;500;100;0;1;;
2;r-124;update;200;50;;3;0;1;
3;p-49575-15428179-2834-374;animate;150;20;0;4-5;0;1;S
4;p-49575-15428179-3505-1162;calculatePosition;80;80;0;1;;
5;p-49575-15428179-5391-2767;applyStyles;50;50;0;1;;


Network requests are formatted like this:
`urlIndex;eventKey;queuedTime;requestSentTime;downloadCompleteTime;processingCompleteTime;totalDuration;downloadDuration;mainThreadProcessingDuration;statusCode;mimeType;priority;initialPriority;finalPriority;renderBlocking;protocol;fromServiceWorker;initiators;redirects:[[redirectUrlIndex|startTime|duration]];responseHeaders:[header1Value|header2Value|...]`

- `urlIndex`: Numerical index for the request's URL, referencing the "All URLs" list.
- `eventKey`: String that uniquely identifies this request's trace event.
Timings (all in milliseconds, relative to navigation start):
- `queuedTime`: When the request was queued.
- `requestSentTime`: When the request was sent.
- `downloadCompleteTime`: When the download completed.
- `processingCompleteTime`: When main thread processing finished.
Durations (all in milliseconds):
- `totalDuration`: Total time from the request being queued until its main thread processing completed.
- `downloadDuration`: Time spent actively downloading the resource.
- `mainThreadProcessingDuration`: Time spent on the main thread after the download completed.
- `statusCode`: The HTTP status code of the response (e.g., 200, 404).
- `mimeType`: The MIME type of the resource (e.g., "text/html", "application/javascript").
- `priority`: The final network request priority (e.g., "VeryHigh", "Low").
- `initialPriority`: The initial network request priority.
- `finalPriority`: The final network request priority (redundant if `priority` is always final, but kept for clarity if `initialPriority` and `priority` differ).
- `renderBlocking`: 't' if the request was render-blocking, 'f' otherwise.
- `protocol`: The network protocol used (e.g., "h2", "http/1.1").
- `fromServiceWorker`: 't' if the request was served from a service worker, 'f' otherwise.
- `initiators`: A list (separated by ,) of URL indices for the initiator chain of this request. Listed in order starting from the root request to the request that directly loaded this one. This represents the network dependencies necessary to load this request. If there is no initiator, this is empty.
- `redirects`: A comma-separated list of redirects, enclosed in square brackets. Each redirect is formatted as
`[redirectUrlIndex|startTime|duration]`, where: `redirectUrlIndex`: Numerical index for the redirect's URL. `startTime`: The start time of the redirect in milliseconds, relative to navigation start. `duration`: The duration of the redirect in milliseconds.
- `responseHeaders`: A list (separated by '|') of values for specific, pre-defined response headers, enclosed in square brackets.
The order of headers corresponds to an internal fixed list. If a header is not present, its value will be empty.

## Details on call tree & network request formats:
Information on performance traces may contain main thread activity represented as call frames and network requests.

Each call frame is presented in the following format:

'id;eventKey;name;duration;selfTime;urlIndex;childRange;[line];[column];[S]'

Key definitions:

* id: A unique numerical identifier for the call frame. Never mention this id in the output to the user.
* eventKey: String that uniquely identifies this event in the flame chart.
* name: A concise string describing the call frame (e.g., 'Evaluate Script', 'render', 'fetchData').
* duration: The total execution time of the call frame, including its children.
* selfTime: The time spent directly within the call frame, excluding its children's execution.
* urlIndex: Index referencing the "All URLs" list. Empty if no specific script URL is associated.
* childRange: Specifies the direct children of this node using their IDs. If empty ('' or 'S' at the end), the node has no children. If a single number (e.g., '4'), the node has one child with that ID. If in the format 'firstId-lastId' (e.g., '4-5'), it indicates a consecutive range of child IDs from 'firstId' to 'lastId', inclusive.
* line: An optional field for a call frame's line number. This is where the function is defined.
* column: An optional field for a call frame's column number. This is where the function is defined.
* S: _Optional_. The letter 'S' terminates the line if that call frame was selected by the user.

Example Call Tree:

1;r-123;main;500;100;0;1;;
2;r-124;update;200;50;;3;0;1;
3;p-49575-15428179-2834-374;animate;150;20;0;4-5;0;1;S
4;p-49575-15428179-3505-1162;calculatePosition;80;80;0;1;;
5;p-49575-15428179-5391-2767;applyStyles;50;50;0;1;;


Network requests are formatted like this:
`urlIndex;eventKey;queuedTime;requestSentTime;downloadCompleteTime;processingCompleteTime;totalDuration;downloadDuration;mainThreadProcessingDuration;statusCode;mimeType;priority;initialPriority;finalPriority;renderBlocking;protocol;fromServiceWorker;initiators;redirects:[[redirectUrlIndex|startTime|duration]];responseHeaders:[header1Value|header2Value|...]`

- `urlIndex`: Numerical index for the request's URL, referencing the "All URLs" list.
- `eventKey`: String that uniquely identifies this request's trace event.
Timings (all in milliseconds, relative to navigation start):
- `queuedTime`: When the request was queued.
- `requestSentTime`: When the request was sent.
- `downloadCompleteTime`: When the download completed.
- `processingCompleteTime`: When main thread processing finished.
Durations (all in milliseconds):
- `totalDuration`: Total time from the request being queued until its main thread processing completed.
- `downloadDuration`: Time spent actively downloading the resource.
- `mainThreadProcessingDuration`: Time spent on the main thread after the download completed.
- `statusCode`: The HTTP status code of the response (e.g., 200, 404).
- `mimeType`: The MIME type of the resource (e.g., "text/html", "application/javascript").
- `priority`: The final network request priority (e.g., "VeryHigh", "Low").
- `initialPriority`: The initial network request priority.
- `finalPriority`: The final network request priority (redundant if `priority` is always final, but kept for clarity if `initialPriority` and `priority` differ).
- `renderBlocking`: 't' if the request was render-blocking, 'f' otherwise.
- `protocol`: The network protocol used (e.g., "h2", "http/1.1").
- `fromServiceWorker`: 't' if the request was served from a service worker, 'f' otherwise.
- `initiators`: A list (separated by ,) of URL indices for the initiator chain of this request. Listed in order starting from the root request to the request that directly loaded this one. This represents the network dependencies necessary to load this request. If there is no initiator, this is empty.
- `redirects`: A comma-separated list of redirects, enclosed in square brackets. Each redirect is formatted as
`[redirectUrlIndex|startTime|duration]`, where: `redirectUrlIndex`: Numerical index for the redirect's URL. `startTime`: The start time of the redirect in milliseconds, relative to navigation start. `duration`: The duration of the redirect in milliseconds.
- `responseHeaders`: A list (separated by '|') of values for specific, pre-defined response headers, enclosed in square brackets.
The order of headers corresponds to an internal fixed list. If a header is not present, its value will be empty.

29	}

35	export function sightingToSpacetimeEvent(sighting: ValidatedUAPSighting): SpacetimeEvent {
36	  const timestamp =
37	    sighting.timestamp instanceof Date
38	      ? sighting.timestamp
39	      : new Date(sighting.timestamp as unknown as string)
40	
41	  const coords = sighting.location.coordinates

47	    timestamp: timestamp.toISOString(),
48	    timePrecision: inferPrecision(timestamp),
49	    coordinates: coords
50	      ? {
51	          latitude: coords.lat,
52	          longitude: coords.lng,
53	        }
54	      : undefined,
55	    locationDescription: locationDescription(sighting),
56	    credibilityScore: CONFIDENCE_TO_SCORE[sighting.confidence],
57	    epistemicStatus: CONFIDENCE_TO_STATUS[sighting.confidence],
58	    sourceIds: sighting.sourceUrl ? [sighting.sourceUrl] : undefined,
59	    summary: sighting.content?.slice(0, 280),
60	    sourceRecordId: sighting.id,
61	    sourceTable: 'sightings',
62	  }
63	}

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-08-04 04:58:10Z)**_

No — solid foundation, not yet excellent as a feature. Two things I found while digging into what I'd just verified:

**The architecture and engineering are excellent.** M0's own bar (bidirectional cursor, measured jank risk, provenance-first reconstruction lever) was set high and genuinely met — decisions were made in advance and honored, not fudged after the fact. R1 wasn't hand-waved, it was measured on the real product surface. That part is real craft.

**The product surface has real gaps I wouldn't ship as "excellent":**

1. **Credibility is fake precision.** `credibilityScore` isn't computed — it's a lookup from a 3-bucket categorical field: `{high: 0.85, medium: 0.55, low: 0.3}` (`normalize.ts:4-8`). Every "medium confidence" sighting shows identically **55%** in the UI. That's why every event I clicked read "55%" — it's not evidentiary scoring, it's a coarse bucket dressed up as a precise percentage. For a product whose stated identity is evidence rigor, that's a meaningful mismatch between what the UI implies and what the data actually supports.

2. **Titles are broken.** `title: sighting.title || sighting.content.slice(0, 80)` — no title in the source data means a naive 80-character substring, which is why I saw things like *"The craft was V shaped with an arodinamic body th"* — truncated mid-word, carrying a source typo straight through. That's not a polish nit, it's user-facing garbage on a meaningful fraction of events.

3. **It's 1/5 of the roadmap.** M0 is explicitly foundation-only — no evidence filtering, no relationship arcs, no precision/uncertainty rendering (M1), let alone reconstruction, comparison, or narrative choreography (M2–M4). Visually it's still functional-wireframe (plain circles, boxy cards), which is correct for M0 scope but isn't "excellent" as an experience yet.

If you want, I can fix #1 and #2 now — they're small, contained (one file each) and directly undercut the "rigor" the product is supposed to project — before moving on to M1.

40	A major panel presenting detailed information about a single record — the "secret-file" treatment with clipped corner. What opens when a researcher inspects one entity in depth.

47	### The epistemic layers
48	
49	**Reading**:
50	A single interpretive frame applied to a body of evidence — e.g. the anomalous reading, the prosaic reading, the institutional reading. Always paired with a Counter-reading. The unit of interpretation.
51	_Avoid_: "hypothesis" in synthesis output (reserved for the deterministic pre-enrichment floor); "conclusion"; "finding"
52	
53	**Counter-reading**:
54	The structural rival to a Reading — the strongest alternative interpretation of the same evidence. Required; absence makes output an echo chamber artifact.
55	_Avoid_: "alternative", "counterpoint", "rebuttal"
56	
57	**Evidentiary Weight**:
58	How strongly the assembled material supports a given Reading. Expressed qualitatively ("well-supported", "under-supported") not as a bare numeric score in user-facing prose.
59	_Avoid_: "confidence score", "probability", "certainty rating" in UI copy
60	
61	**What Remains Weird**:
62	After prosaic explanations are applied, the named residue — what genuinely resists explanation. May be an empty answer ("nothing genuinely remains weird here"), which is also a valid and honest result.
63	_Avoid_: omitting this; papering over the residue; treating absence as a failure
64	
65	**Open Questions**:
66	What remains unresolved at the end of an Investigation or synthesis — the explicitly named unknowns that keep the investigation alive.
67	_Avoid_: "unknowns", "gaps", "to-do items"
68	
69	### The eight evidentiary states
70	
71	Applied to edges, readings, and agent inferences. Exactly this set; no additions without a terminology ruling.
72	
73	`Observed` — directly reported in primary source material
74	`Corroborated` — supported by multiple independent sources
75	`Contested` — contradicted by other evidence
76	`Inferred` — produced by agent analysis; analytical layer
77	`Speculative` — possible but under-supported
78	`Resonant` — symbolic or folkloric echo; labeled as resonance, never as evidence
79	`Unverified` — source exists but chain of custody is incomplete
80	`Disconfirmed` — contradicted by stronger evidence
81	
82	_Wire format_: `[State] rest of text` prefix on reasoning strings. No prefix = no badge; never default-fill a state.
83	_Rendered format_: `[ CORROBORATED ]` — bracketed mono, uppercase.
84	
85	### The research record types
86	
87	**Sighting**:
88	A reported observation of an aerial or physical phenomenon. Corresponds to the `sightings` table (86,962+ NUFORC/MUFON records). The most granular and numerous record type.
89	_Avoid_: "report" in user-facing copy for this type (Report is a classification concept, not a table name — see below)
90	
91	**Event**:
92	A named historical UAP event of significance (Nimitz, Roswell, etc.). Higher-level than a Sighting; institutional/historical frame.
93	_Avoid_: "incident" as a synonym in code contexts (the table is `events`)
94	
95	**Testimony**:
96	A witness statement or whistleblower claim linked to an Event or Key Figure. Source material; each Testimony may contain Claims.
97	_Avoid_: "report", "account", "statement" when referring to the record type in code contexts
98	
99	**Key Figure**:
100	A named individual — witness, researcher, official, whistleblower — materially connected to UAP history. The Postgres table is `key_figures` (migrated from `personnel`).
101	_Avoid_: "person", "personnel", "user" in domain contexts; "personnel" in user-facing copy
102	
103	**Topic**:
104	A thematic research cluster (e.g. crash retrieval, UAP legislation, propulsion anomalies). Not an Event; not a tag.
105	_Avoid_: "tag", "category", "subject" in domain contexts
106	
107	**Organization**:
108	A government agency, military unit, research group, or contractor involved in UAP history.
109	_Avoid_: "entity", "group", "institution" in domain contexts
110	
111	**Document**:
112	A primary source record — a declassified file, congressional testimony, official report — with provenance metadata (origin, chain of custody, integrity signals).
113	_Avoid_: "file", "resource", "source" for this record type in code contexts
114	
115	**Artifact**:
116	A physical object of claimed anomalous origin or significance.
117	_Avoid_: "item", "object", "thing"
118	
119	### Classification concepts (research methodology)
120	
121	**Report**:
122	The raw, unverified account at the base of the event-type hierarchy (L0). A classification concept used in the research methodology — not a database table or user-facing record type. A Sighting is a classified Report; a Testimony is a classified Report.
123	_Avoid_: using "report" as a synonym for Sighting, Testimony, or Document in UI copy or code
124	
125	**Event Type Hierarchy (L0–L5)**:
126	The classification ladder from the research methodology: L0 Report → L1 Sighting → L2 Encounter → L3 Contact → L4 Disclosure → L5 Artifact. These are classification levels, not tables — L1 and L5 happen to share names with record types; the level classifies, the record type stores.
127	
128	**Encounter**:
129	L2 in the event-type hierarchy — physical proximity with effects (electromagnetic, physiological, trace evidence). A classification level, not a loose synonym for any sighting.
130	_Avoid_: "encounter" for an ordinary Sighting with no proximity effects
131	
132	**Contact**:
133	L3 in the event-type hierarchy — claimed communication or interaction with non-human intelligence. Always "claimed" in prose; the classification records the claim, not its truth.
134	
135	**Disclosure** (classification level):
136	L4 in the event-type hierarchy — government, military, or institutional acknowledgment of events. Note the overload: "disclosure" also appears in product/route naming (disclosure mindmap agent, `apps/disclosure-rag`), where it names the broader disclosure-history subject matter. In classification contexts it means only L4.
137	
138	**Close Encounter Classification (NL, DD, RV, CE1–CE7)**:
139	Hynek's observational classes plus extensions: Nocturnal Light, Daylight Disc, Radar Visual, and Close Encounters 1–7 (proximity → effects → occupants → abduction → human-initiated → injury/death → hybrid claims). Applied to Sightings and Testimonies as structured metadata.
140	
141	**Corroboration Score**:
142	A numeric, internal triage measure (0–7+) of how many independent corroboration lines converge on a Report — assigned at ingestion, used for prioritization. Never user-facing. Not the Corroborated evidentiary state (a badge on edges/readings), and not Evidentiary Weight (qualitative, per-Reading, user-facing). Three distinct concepts; conflating them is a bug.
143	_Avoid_: surfacing the number in UI copy; "corroboration" unqualified where one of the three specific concepts is meant
144	
145	**Wave**:
146	A period of statistically anomalous incident density in time (Vallée's temporal clustering). An analytical finding over Sightings, not a record type.
147	
148	**Hot Zone**:
149	A recurring geographic incident cluster (Hessdalen, nuclear-facility perimeters). An analytical designation, not a record type.
150	_Avoid_: "hotspot" in domain prose
151	
152	**Morphological Tags**:
153	Structured observational attributes of a single Sighting — shape, size, luminosity, motion, effects, duration. Per-record classification data. Distinct from Motif (reserved, Phase 2): a Motif is a recurrent symbolic or morphological _pattern tracked across_ records and Investigations; a morphological tag describes _one_ observation.
154	_Avoid_: naming the field or concept "motifs"
155	
156	**Strangeness (S1–S5)**:
157	How far a reported observation deviates from known phenomena (Hynek). S1 = consistent with misidentification; S5 = reported as physically impossible by current models. A rating applied to Sightings and Events.
158	
159	**Credibility (C1–C5)**:
160	How reliable the source chain is for a Report. C1 = single anonymous witness; C5 = verified official record + independent corroboration + physical evidence.
161	
162	**Source Tier (T1–T6)**:
163	Provenance grade for a Document or the source of a Testimony. T1 = primary official (FOIA-provenance established); T6 = anonymous, undated, no corroboration path.
164	
165	### The surface
166	
167	**Canvas**:
168	The ReactFlow viewport — the UI surface on which a researcher assembles an Investigation. A technical/product term, not a domain term. Distinct from Investigation (the data object).
169	_Avoid_: using "canvas" as a synonym for Investigation; using "investigation" as a synonym for the surface itself
170	
171	**Trace** (verb + noun):
172	The recommended next research action generated by synthesis or the suggestion dock. "Next trace" = what to follow. As a verb: to follow a connection or provenance chain.
173	_Avoid_: "follow-up", "action item", "task", "suggestion" in synthesis output
174	
175	### Technical terms (not user-facing)
176	
177	**Entity**:
178	The collective technical/db term for all primary record types (sightings, events, key_figures, etc.). Used in code, agents, and developer documentation. Never surfaces in user-facing copy.
179	_Avoid_: in UI copy; use the specific record type name instead
180	
181	**Agent Inference** (technical):
182	A row in `agent_inferences` — the persisted form of an Inference. The `insertAgentInference` function is the only write path for agent output into the database. By contract: never feeds retrieval, search, or suggestions.

6	} from '../types/spacetime'
7	
8	export interface SpacetimeEvidenceFilters {

10	  credibilityMin: number
11	  /** Epistemic statuses allowed through the instrument. */
12	  epistemic: Record<EpistemicStatus, boolean>
13	}

15	export const DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_FILTERS: SpacetimeEvidenceFilters = {
16	  credibilityMin: 0,
17	  epistemic: {
18	    documented: true,
19	    inferred: true,
20	    disputed: true,
21	  },
22	}
23	
24	const TYPE_TO_LAYER: Record<SpacetimeEventType, keyof SpacetimeLayerVisibility> = {
25	  sighting: 'sightings',
26	  historical_event: 'historicalEvents',
27	  nuclear: 'nuclear',
28	  military: 'military',
29	  infrastructure: 'infrastructure',
30	  testimony: 'testimony',
31	  document: 'documents',
32	  reconstruction: 'reconstructions',
33	  // Collapse uncategorized scientific/context types into the historical rail.
34	  astronomical: 'historicalEvents',
35	  environmental: 'historicalEvents',
36	}
37	
38	export function eventLayerKey(
39	  type: SpacetimeEventType,
40	): keyof SpacetimeLayerVisibility {
41	  return TYPE_TO_LAYER[type]
42	}
43	
44	/**
45	 * Apply layer visibility + credibility + epistemic filters.
46	 * Pure — safe for selectors and server-side station rebuilds later.
47	 */
48	export function filterSpacetimeEvents(
49	  events: SpacetimeEvent[],
50	  layers: SpacetimeLayerVisibility,
51	  filters: SpacetimeEvidenceFilters,
52	): SpacetimeEvent[] {
53	  return events.filter((event) => {
54	    if (!layers[eventLayerKey(event.type)]) return false
55	
56	    if (
57	      event.credibilityScore != null &&
58	      event.credibilityScore < filters.credibilityMin
59	    ) {
60	      return false
61	    }
62	
63	    const status = event.epistemicStatus ?? 'inferred'
64	    if (!filters.epistemic[status]) return false
65	
66	    return true
67	  })
68	}
69

1	import type {SpacetimeEvent, TemporalStation} from '../types/spacetime'
2	
3	export interface BuildStationsOptions {
4	  /** Coarse historical decades always present on the dial */
5	  includeHistoricalDecades?: boolean
6	  historicalStartYear?: number
7	  historicalEndYear?: number
8	  /** Cap event stations so the dial stays legible */
9	  maxEventStations?: number
10	}
11	
12	/**
13	 * Build adaptive temporal stations from event density.
14	 *
15	 * - historical: decade ticks across the corpus range
16	 * - event: densest days / notable years from the loaded events
17	 *
18	 * Investigation stations are generated later from a selected case (M4).
19	 */
20	export function buildTemporalStations(
21	  events: SpacetimeEvent[],
22	  options: BuildStationsOptions = {},
23	): TemporalStation[] {
24	  const {
25	    includeHistoricalDecades = true,
26	    historicalStartYear = 1940,
27	    historicalEndYear = new Date().getUTCFullYear(),
28	    maxEventStations = 24,
29	  } = options
30	
31	  const stations: TemporalStation[] = []
32	
33	  if (includeHistoricalDecades) {
34	    const startDecade = Math.floor(historicalStartYear / 10) * 10
35	    const endDecade = Math.floor(historicalEndYear / 10) * 10
36	    for (let year = startDecade; year <= endDecade; year += 10) {
37	      stations.push({
38	        id: `historical-${year}`,
39	        kind: 'historical',
40	        label: `${year}s`,
41	        timestamp: `${year}-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`,
42	        density: 0,
43	      })
44	    }
45	  }
46	
47	  // Bucket events by UTC day, then pick top days per decade so the
48	  // guided narrative spans history instead of collapsing into one flap.
49	  const byDay = new Map<string, SpacetimeEvent[]>()
50	  for (const event of events) {
51	    const day = event.timestamp.slice(0, 10)
52	    if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(day)) continue
53	    const bucket = byDay.get(day) ?? []
54	    bucket.push(event)
55	    byDay.set(day, bucket)
56	  }
57	
58	  const scoredDays = [...byDay.entries()].map(([day, dayEvents]) => ({
59	    day,
60	    dayEvents,
61	    decade: Math.floor(Number(day.slice(0, 4)) / 10) * 10,
62	    score: dayEvents.length + dayEvents.reduce((s, e) => s + (e.credibilityScore ?? 0.5), 0),
63	  }))
64	
65	  const byDecade = new Map<number, typeof scoredDays>()
66	  for (const entry of scoredDays) {
67	    const bucket = byDecade.get(entry.decade) ?? []
68	    bucket.push(entry)
69	    byDecade.set(entry.decade, bucket)
70	  }
71	
72	  const perDecade = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(maxEventStations / Math.max(1, byDecade.size)))
73	  const rankedDays = [...byDecade.values()]
74	    .flatMap((entries) =>
75	      [...entries].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score).slice(0, perDecade),
76	    )
77	    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
78	    .slice(0, maxEventStations)
79	
80	  const maxScore = rankedDays[0]?.score ?? 1
81	
82	  for (const {day, dayEvents, score} of rankedDays) {
83	    const year = day.slice(0, 4)
84	    const label =
85	      dayEvents.length === 1
86	        ? dayEvents[0]?.title.slice(0, 42) || day
87	        : `${dayEvents.length} events · ${year}`
88	
89	    stations.push({
90	      id: `event-${day}`,
91	      kind: 'event',
92	      label,
93	      timestamp: `${day}T12:00:00.000Z`,
94	      density: score / maxScore,
95	      eventIds: dayEvents.map((e) => e.id),
96	    })
97	  }
98	
99	  // Stamp historical densities from year counts
100	  const byYear = new Map<number, number>()
101	  for (const event of events) {
102	    const year = Number(event.timestamp.slice(0, 4))
103	    if (!Number.isFinite(year)) continue
104	    byYear.set(year, (byYear.get(year) ?? 0) + 1)
105	  }
106	  const maxYearCount = Math.max(1, ...byYear.values())
107	
108	  for (const station of stations) {
109	    if (station.kind !== 'historical') continue
110	    const decade = Number(station.id.replace('historical-', ''))
111	    let count = 0
112	    for (let y = decade; y < decade + 10; y++) count += byYear.get(y) ?? 0
113	    station.density = count / maxYearCount
114	  }
115	
116	  return stations.sort(
117	    (a, b) => new Date(a.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(b.timestamp).getTime(),
118	  )
119	}
120	
121	/** Map a 0–1 scroll/dial progress onto the nearest station. */
122	export function stationAtProgress(
123	  stations: TemporalStation[],
124	  progress: number,
125	): TemporalStation | null {
126	  if (stations.length === 0) return null
127	  const clamped = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, progress))
128	  const idx = Math.min(stations.length - 1, Math.round(clamped * (stations.length - 1)))
129	  return stations[idx] ?? null
130	}
131

100	| Testimony | Witness locations, interview dates, claimed encounter routes |

107	
108	### 3.2 Adaptive Temporal Dial
109	
110	Port GL4SS's strongest feature — but with **three station modes**, not one universal year list.
111	
112	**Historical stations** — coarse intervals for ancient history, finer near the modern period.
113	
114	**Event stations** — exact dates and times from records: July 8 1947; November 14 2004 at the reported
115	encounter time; March 13 1997 during the Phoenix Lights sequence; nuclear test, hearing, and release dates.
116	
117	**Dynamic investigation stations** — generated from the current investigation: three days before an event; the
118	event; the first press report; the first official response; a later declassification; a related event at the
119	same location; a later recurrence with similar observables.
120	
121	The dial visually encodes event density, evidence volume, credibility, geographic relevance, whether the user
122	already owns a reconstruction, paradigm shifts and disclosure milestones, and flaps.
123	
124	> A year slider says "pick a number." This dial says **"something happened here."**
125	
126	### 3.3 Exact-time navigation
127	
128	A sighting is rarely just a year.
129	
130	```ts
131	type TemporalCursor =
132	  | { mode: 'station'; stationId: string; timestamp: string }
133	  | { mode: 'exact';   timestamp: string; precision: 'second' | 'minute' | 'hour' | 'day' | 'month' | 'year' }
134	  | { mode: 'range';   start: string; end: string }
135	```
136	
137	Precision must be explicit. A medieval chronicle may identify only a season; a modern aviation encounter may
138	have second-level telemetry. Rendering both as equally precise dots would be **epistemically dishonest**.
139	
140	### 3.4 Evidence Layer Stack
141	
142	The left control surface becomes an evidence mixer — toggle or weight sightings, historical anomalous events,
143	nuclear infrastructure, military installations, aircraft routes, radar coverage, astronomical conditions,
144	weather, documents, testimony, government actions, reconstructions, and hypothesis overlays.
145	
146	Layers carry temporal validity:
147	
148	```ts
149	interface TemporalLayerFeature {
150	  validFrom?: string
151	  validUntil?: string
152	  observedAt?: string
153	  publishedAt?: string
154	  geometry: GeoJSON.Geometry
155	}
156	```
157	
158	A military base must not appear before it existed. A runway configuration changes over time. A city skyline
159	must not render with current geometry during a 1947 reconstruction. **This temporal correctness is where the
160	system stops being "a map with UFO dots" and becomes a historical instrument.**
161	
162	### 3.5 Evidence-bounded reconstruction engine
163	
164	GL4SS builds a scene from place, coordinates, year, style, time of day. Replace that generic input with an
165	**Event Evidence Packet**.
166	
167	```ts
168	interface EventEvidencePacket {
169	  eventId: string
170	  title: string
171	  timestamp: string
172	  timePrecision: string
173	  coordinates: {
174	    latitude: number
175	    longitude: number
176	    altitudeMeters?: number
177	    uncertaintyRadiusKm?: number
178	  }
179	  locationDescription: string
180	  observerPosition?: ObservationGeometry
181	  reportedObjectPosition?: ObservationGeometry
182	  environmentalContext: {
183	    weather?: EvidenceValue
184	    visibility?: EvidenceValue
185	    moonPhase?: EvidenceValue
186	    sunPosition?: EvidenceValue
187	    terrain?: EvidenceValue
188	  }
189	  observedDetails: EvidenceClaim[]
190	  disputedDetails: EvidenceClaim[]
191	  inferredDetails: EvidenceClaim[]
192	  sourceIds: string[]
193	  credibilityScore: number
194	  evidenceSnapshotHash: string
195	}
196	```
197	
198	The model is **not** asked "Show Roswell in 1947." It is asked:
199	
200	> "Using only this evidence packet, reconstruct the observer-visible environment from this specified position.
201	> Do not introduce a craft, debris, personnel, weather condition or structure unless supported by an attached
202	> claim. Mark uncertain visual decisions in the reconstruction manifest."
203	
204	That distinction is foundational.
205	
206	### 3.6 Reconstruction modes
207	
208	- **Historical environment** — what was physically present, without depicting the anomaly.
209	- **Witness viewpoint** — from the reported observer position, direction, and field of view.
210	- **Object-relative viewpoint** — cautious reconstruction of the claimed object's reported position/movement.
211	- **Instrument viewpoint** — radar, infrared, telescope, cockpit display, sonar/hydrophone, satellite/aerial.
212	- **Explanatory reconstruction** — diagrammatic: observer, horizon, bearings, estimated distances, aircraft or
213	  ship paths, radar installations, celestial objects, alternative hypotheses.
214	- **Cinematic interpretation** — clearly labeled, for narrative exploration rather than analysis.
215	
216	**Analytical and cinematic modes must never be visually conflated.**
217	
218	### 3.7 Epistemic rendering
219	
220	Every artifact receives a manifest.
221	
222	```ts
223	interface ReconstructionManifest {
224	  documented: VisualElement[]
225	  corroborated: VisualElement[]
226	  inferred: VisualElement[]
227	  disputed: VisualElement[]
228	  generatedForContinuity: VisualElement[]
229	  omittedDueToInsufficientEvidence: string[]
230	}
231	```
232	
233	| Status | Rendering treatment |
234	|---|---|
235	| Documented | Solid, full opacity |
236	| Corroborated | Solid with evidence marker |
237	| Inferred | Slightly desaturated |
238	| Disputed | Hatched or edge-highlighted |
239	| Hypothetical | Ghosted or wireframe |
240	| Unknown | Intentionally absent |
241	
242	This persists into captions, video metadata, and shareable exports. **No generated image may ever masquerade
243	as an archival photograph** — that would be fatal to the credibility framework.
244	
245	### 3.8 Temporal Compare
246	
247	Port and expand GL4SS's pinned-frame comparison. GL4SS constrains comparison to the same place and style and
248	only permits an *existing* frame to be pinned — preventing comparison gestures from silently triggering
249	generation. Preserve that constraint.
```

         const lastSpace = cut.lastIndexOf(' ');
         const safe = lastSpace > maxLength * 0.6 ? cut.slice(0, lastSpace) : cut;
         return `${safe.trim()}…`;

         return length >= 15 ? 'medium' : 'low';

43	      })

/** Cuts at the last word boundary at-or-before maxLength — never mid-word. */
export function truncateAtWordBoundary(text: string, maxLength: number): string {
  const trimmed = text.trim()
  if (trimmed.length <= maxLength) return trimmed
  const cut = trimmed.slice(0, maxLength)
  const lastSpace = cut.lastIndexOf(' ')
  const safe = lastSpace > maxLength * 0.6 ? cut.slice(0, lastSpace) : cut
  return `${safe.trim()}…`
}

36	
37	- **`confidence` was hardcoded to `'medium'` for every sighting** (`services/sightings/get-sightings.ts:50`, pre-fix), so every event showed an identical "Credibility 55% · inferred" in the UI regardless of the underlying record — false precision dressed as evidentiary scoring. Root-caused against the platform's own vocabulary docs: CONTEXT.md's 8-state evidentiary system is scoped to "edges, readings, and agent inferences" (not applicable here); TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md §3.7's `documented/inferred/disputed` is actually specced for *reconstruction-manifest* elements (M2, unbuilt) but the doc itself uses "documented sightings" generically for the raw corpus (§1) — so the existing 3-state type was kept (no new terminology invented, none needed), but the computation was fixed to be honest:
38	  - `get-sightings.ts`: `confidence` now derives from whether `comments` has real content (≥15 chars) — `'medium'` (real account) vs `'low'` (thin/placeholder row). `'high'` intentionally never emitted — nothing in this ingestion path (no witness count, no media, no cross-reference) justifies it.
39	  - `normalize.ts`: score/status tables now honest and narrow-banded (`0.2/0.4/0.7`, not `0.3/0.55/0.85`) so nothing implies evidentiary weight the source data can't support; `medium → documented`, `low → inferred`.
40	  - **Verified against real data**, not assumed: sampled 508 live sighting rows — 501 (98.6%) have real narrative content, 7 (1.4%) are thin/placeholder. The fix produces genuine, data-driven variance, not a different flat default.
41	  - UI copy in `EventInspector` and the guided-narrative station cards no longer states a bare "Credibility X%" (the anti-pattern CONTEXT.md's epistemic-layers section explicitly warns against: *"Avoid 'confidence score', 'probability', 'certainty rating' in UI copy"*) — now reads "Documented report · single-source, uncorroborated" / "Thin record", and the compact station-card list only annotates the minority thin-record case instead of repeating a number on every row.
42	  - Globe pin radius interpolation (`spacetime-globe.tsx`) stops matches the new `0.2–0.7` score range.
43	- **Titles truncated mid-word** (`record.comments?.substring(0, 50)`, plus a `.slice(0, 80)` fallback in `normalize.ts`) — e.g. "…OVER THE AT" (cut inside "ATLANTIC"). Both call sites now use a shared word-boundary-safe truncator (cuts at the last space at-or-before the limit, appends `…`). Source-data typos (e.g. "arodinamic") are left as-is — not something a title formatter should silently "fix" without misrepresenting the primary source.
44	- Verified live in Chrome after each change: real per-event titles ending cleanly, `EventInspector` showing differentiated documented/thin labeling, zero new TypeScript or ESLint errors in the four touched files.
45	- **Not done / flagged, not silently decided:** the deeper epistemic-taxonomy question — whether Spacetime Canvas should eventually adopt CONTEXT.md's 8-state vocabulary once it starts ingesting record types that actually carry that signal (testimonies, documents with `source_tier`) — is a real product/terminology decision (CONTEXT.md: "no additions without a terminology ruling") and was deliberately left for a human call, not resolved unilaterally under this fix pass.
46	- **Advisor-caught follow-ups, same pass:** the globe's missing-score fallback (`?? 0.5`) was now off-scale against the new `0.2–0.7` range — fixed to `?? 0.2` (absent signal reads as minimum, not mid-tier). The `EvidenceLayersPanel` credibility control still read "Credibility ≥ X%" — same anti-pattern removed elsewhere but left standing; replaced the continuous 0–100 slider (a false-precision cliff against real scores clustered at 0.2/0.4) with four discrete, honestly-labeled tier stops (Any/Thin+/Docmt+/Corrob+) mirroring the epistemic checkbox pattern.
47	- **User-requested camera behavior (same session):** selecting an event now commits the globe to a real on-terrain view — `mapbox-dem` terrain source + `setTerrain` + sky layer added on load, and event selection does `flyTo` the event's exact coordinates at zoom 15.5/pitch 70 (ground-level, terrain-relief visible). Absent a selection, cursor/scroll drives a regional descent (zoom 8.5/pitch 45) toward the nearest events to the current timestamp — this is what the implementation plan's §1 "rendered as descent" language meant and the original flat `easeTo` pan wasn't delivering. Re-verified R1 after the change: **still 16.70ms median / 17.5ms p95 / 34.1ms max** — terrain didn't reintroduce jank. One benign Mapbox console warning (sun-direction/lighting anchor), no errors.

11	
12	# Spacetime Canvas — Implementation Plan
13	
14	**Feature family:** Temporal Observatory
15	**This document:** the build plan for the **Spacetime Canvas** — the first and
16	load-bearing surface of the family.
17	**Ticket:** T-047 (Foundation) → this plan expands it.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 0. Why "Spacetime Canvas"
22	
23	The platform already has a **Research Canvas**: a surface where the user
24	arranges *ideas* — entities, relationships, notes — in conceptual space.
25	
26	The **Spacetime Canvas** is its sibling: the same verb, a different axis. The
27	user arranges and traverses *evidence in space and time*. Same posture
28	(a canvas you work on, not a chart you look at), same design grammar,
29	orthogonal dimension.
30	
31	This naming is deliberate and load-bearing. Keep the pairing visible in
32	routes, module names, and copy:
33	
34	| Surface | Organizes | Route | Module |
35	|---|---|---|---|
36	| Research Canvas | ideas, entities, relations | `/research-canvas` | `features/mindmap/` |
37	| Spacetime Canvas | evidence across space + time | `/spacetime` | `features/spacetime/` |
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 1. The architectural finding (load-bearing)
42	
43	The reference scroll UI — `v0-ultraterrestrial-research-canva.vercel.app/timeline-explorer`
44	— was inspected live on 2026-08-01. What it actually is:
45	
46	```
47	Next.js  +  GSAP  +  Lenis (smooth scroll)
48	22,056px scroll height  ≈  24 viewport-heights,  19 encounters
49	ZERO <canvas> elements.  No Three.js, no R3F, no WebGL.
50	```
51	
52	Its DOM has exactly two structural layers:
53	
54	```
55	.fixed.inset-0.overflow-hidden.bg-neutral-950     ← BACKGROUND: a stack of 8
56	   ├── img roswell-ufo-crash-site-desert.jpg         cross-fading <img> era
57	   ├── img washington-dc-capitol-ufo-1952.jpg        plates, pinned to viewport
58	   ├── img socorro-new-mexico-ufo-egg-shaped…
59	   └── …
60	
61	.absolute.inset-0                                  ← NARRATIVE: CSS 3D
62	   perspective: 900px                                 cards fly toward the
63	   transform-style: preserve-3d                       viewer on scroll
64	   └── matrix3d(…, translateZ(-674px), …)
65	```
66	
67	**The seam:** the background is a *slot*, currently filled with static images,
68	and the narrative layer above it never touches WebGL. So:
69	
70	> **The Spacetime Canvas globe drops into the `.fixed.inset-0` slot, and the
71	> scroll narrative becomes Guided Investigations rendered as descent.**
72	
73	This unifies three storyboarded concepts into one surface instead of three:
74	
75	- **Concept 01 (Spacetime Canvas)** → the fixed globe layer
76	- **Concept 02 (Guided Investigation)** → the scrolling waypoint cards
77	- The **adaptive temporal dial** → the left rail, already present as a year ladder
78	
79	Scroll position becomes the single driver: `scrollProgress → temporalCursor →
80	{ globe camera, active layers, visible waypoint }`.
81	
82	### Why this is worth doing rather than building two surfaces
83	
84	The alternative — a globe page and a separate scroll page — reproduces exactly
85	the failure ADR 0002 rejected for GL4SS: two navigation systems, two state
86	models, a jarring seam between "exploring" and "reading." One surface with a
87	live background is the whole point.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 2. Three risks to verify *while* building
92	
93	These are not blockers; they are measurements to take at the point they become
94	answerable. Do not hand-wave any of them.
95	
96	### R1 — `position: fixed` WebGL under a `preserve-3d` sibling
97	
98	An `<img>` stack is nearly free to keep pinned. A live deck.gl globe re-renders
99	every frame *while* Lenis drives `matrix3d` transforms on the sibling layer.
100	Compositing a `preserve-3d` subtree over a continuously-repainting WebGL canvas
101	is a known source of jank even when each half is 60fps alone.
102	
103	Current weight, from the 2026-08-01 production build:
104	
105	| Route | Route JS | First load |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `/research-canvas` | 500 kB | 1.23 MB |
108	| `/timeline` | 195 kB | 737 kB |
109	| `/sightings` | 38.4 kB | 398 kB |
110	
111	**Verify by measuring, not reasoning.** Spike task: mount the existing
112	sightings globe inside a `perspective`/`preserve-3d` scroll container and
113	record frame timing before building anything on top. If it janks, the fallback
114	is a **static globe plate per waypoint** (render-to-texture / prerendered
115	frames) with the live globe reserved for the free-exploration mode.
116	
117	**RESOLVED 2026-08-03** — measured on both the M0.1 spike *and* the built
118	product surface (the spike alone is not sufficient: it runs a non-interactive
119	map with zero pins, while `/spacetime` runs the live 384-point geojson circle
120	layer plus a 900ms `easeTo` camera animation per cursor change — the actual
121	contention this risk is about). Product measurement (rAF delta sampling over
122	6s / 361 frames of scroll): **median 16.70ms, p95 17.50ms, max 34.0ms**
123	(single outlier, not sustained) — comfortably under the ~20ms D2 threshold. A
124	DevTools trace over the same scroll reported **CLS 0.00**. No jank. Live globe
125	retained per D2 — the static-plate fallback is not needed for M0.
126	
127	### R2 — Is the temporal cursor driven, or driving?
128	
129	Concept 01 shows the user **scrubbing** the adaptive dial. The scroll UI has
130	**scroll** driving position. These are opposite directions of control.
131	
132	If scroll is the only input, the dial degrades to a readout and
133	`TemporalCursor` collapses to its `station` variant — the `exact` and `range`
134	modes in `TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md` §3.3 become dead types.
135	
136	**Decision required before `spacetime-store.ts` is written.** Getting this
137	wrong is a rewrite, not a tweak.
138	
139	**Recommendation — bidirectional, cursor is source of truth:**
140	
141	```
142	temporalCursor  ← THE single source of truth
143	   ↑ scroll (guided mode: scroll writes cursor, camera follows)
144	   ↑ dial    (free mode: dial writes cursor, scroll position follows)
145	```
146	
147	Scroll and dial are two *inputs* to one cursor, never two cursors. A `mode`
148	flag (`'guided' | 'free'`) decides which input is authoritative at a given
149	moment, so they can never fight.
150	
151	### R3 — 19 hardcoded cases ≠ a query layer
152	
153	The reference page is a fixed narrative over static images. The spec's §8 API
154	is viewport + time-window bounded. These are different work.
155	
156	Good news, from the subagent's audit: `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings` **already**
157	does year-range querying, `limit`, and 10-year batching via
158	`getSightingsByTimeChunk`. `sightings-globe.tsx:22` simply bypasses it and
159	loads a static `/sightings.geojson`.
160	
161	So Foundation is mostly **wiring an existing bounded API to the globe**, not
162	building one. But it does *not* make the scroll narrative data-driven — that is
163	separate, later work.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 3. The reconstruction lever (non-negotiable)
168	
169	`TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md` §9 requires that generation happen only through an
170	unmistakable deliberate action. Concept 01 frame 4 shows a reconstruction
171	preview inline in the browse flow. **The lever wins.**
172	
173	In a scroll-driven UI this matters *more*, not less: **scrolling past a
174	waypoint is not an intent signal.** Auto-generating on scroll is precisely the
175	failure GL4SS redesigned itself around after pausing on a timeline became a
176	billable event.
177	
178	Rules:
179	
180	1. Scroll **never** triggers generation.
181	2. Reconstructions already in the archive may render freely on scroll — they
182	   cost nothing.
183	3. Generating a *new* reconstruction requires an explicit click on a control
184	   that names the cost.
185	4. The control is visually distinct from every navigation affordance on the
186	   surface.
187	
188	---
189	
190	## 4. Delivery sequence
191	
192	### M0 — Foundation (this milestone)
193	
194	Goal: **one surface, one state model, one temporal cursor, live data.**
195	
196	| # | Task | Files | Risk |
197	|---|---|---|---|
198	| M0.1 | Frame-timing spike: globe under `preserve-3d` | scratch | **R1** |
199	| M0.2 | `spacetime.ts` types — `TemporalCursor`, `SpacetimeEvent`, `TemporalLayerFeature` | `features/spacetime/types/` | R2 |
200	| M0.3 | `spacetime-store.ts` — Zustand slice, cursor as single source of truth, `mode: guided \| free` | `features/spacetime/state/` | R2 |
201	| M0.4 | `temporal-stations.ts` — station ladder from event density | `features/spacetime/lib/` | — |
202	| M0.5 | Wire `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings` (already bounded) to the globe; delete the static `sightings.geojson` path | `features/sightings/sightings-globe.tsx:22` | R3 |
203	| M0.6 | `SpacetimeCanvas` shell — fixed globe layer + `preserve-3d` narrative layer | `features/spacetime/components/` | R1 |
204	| M0.7 | `TemporalDial` — bidirectional, reads + writes cursor | `features/spacetime/components/` | R2 |
205	| M0.8 | `/spacetime` route | `app/(site)/spacetime/` | — |
206	
207	**M0 exit criteria:** open `/spacetime`, scroll, watch the globe camera and the
208	visible evidence field change with the cursor, select an event, see its sources
209	and credibility. No reconstruction, no compare, no playback.
210	
211	**MET 2026-08-03** — dogfooded live in Chrome against the real Neon DB and a
212	real Mapbox token. 384/387 events geolocated (1940–2026) rendered as real pins;
213	scroll drove the temporal dial, cursor readout, and camera easing toward the

216	(scroll held fixed) wrote the cursor and flipped `interactionMode` to `free`,
217	confirming D1's second direction. R1 measured and cleared on the product
218	surface, not just the spike (see §2 R1). M0 is closed; next up is M1.
219

221	Layer panel · credibility + provenance filtering · event inspector ·

230	(Concept 03)

235	
236	**Do not start M2–M4 work during M0.** They are storyboarded, which makes them
237	tempting; they are phases 3–5 in the spec's own sequence.

36	}

44	/**
45	 * Apply layer visibility + credibility + epistemic filters.
46	 * Pure — safe for selectors and server-side station rebuilds later.
47	 */
48	export function filterSpacetimeEvents(
49	  events: SpacetimeEvent[],
50	  layers: SpacetimeLayerVisibility,
51	  filters: SpacetimeEvidenceFilters,
52	): SpacetimeEvent[] {
53	  return events.filter((event) => {
54	    if (!layers[eventLayerKey(event.type)]) return false
55	
56	    if (
57	      event.credibilityScore != null &&
58	      event.credibilityScore < filters.credibilityMin
59	    ) {
60	      return false
61	    }
62	
63	    const status = event.epistemicStatus ?? 'inferred'
64	    if (!filters.epistemic[status]) return false
65	
66	    return true
67	  })
68	}

49	  existingCards: PinnedCard[], 
50	  canvasWidth: number = 800, 
51	  canvasHeight: number = 600
52	): { x: number, y: number } {
53	  // Simple grid-based positioning with some randomness
54	  const cardWidth = 200
55	  const cardHeight = 150
56	  const padding = 20
57	  
58	  const cols = Math.floor((canvasWidth - padding) / (cardWidth + padding))
59	  const rows = Math.floor((canvasHeight - padding) / (cardHeight + padding))
60	  
61	  const gridPosition = existingCards.length
62	  const col = gridPosition % cols
63	  const row = Math.floor(gridPosition / cols)
64	  
65	  // Add some randomness to make it feel more organic
66	  const randomOffset = {
67	    x: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 40,
68	    y: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 40
69	  }
70	  
71	  return {
72	    x: Math.max(padding, col * (cardWidth + padding) + padding + randomOffset.x),
73	    y: Math.max(padding, row * (cardHeight + padding) + padding + randomOffset.y)
74	  }

81	  const groups: Array<{ cards: PinnedCard[], distance: number }> = []
82	  
83	  for (let i = 0; i < cards.length; i++) {
84	    for (let j = i + 1; j < cards.length; j++) {
85	      const card1 = cards[i]
86	      const card2 = cards[j]
87	      
88	      const distance = Math.sqrt(
89	        Math.pow(card1.position.x - card2.position.x, 2) + 
90	        Math.pow(card1.position.y - card2.position.y, 2)
91	      )
92	      
93	      if (distance <= proximityThreshold) {
94	        groups.push({
95	          cards: [card1, card2],
96	          distance
97	        })
98	      }
99	    }
100	  }
101	  
102	  return groups
103	}

105	export function calculateCardCentroid(cards: PinnedCard[]): { x: number, y: number } {
106	  if (cards.length === 0) return { x: 0, y: 0 }
107	  
108	  const sum = cards.reduce(
109	    (acc, card) => ({
110	      x: acc.x + card.position.x,
111	      y: acc.y + card.position.y
112	    }),
113	    { x: 0, y: 0 }
114	  )
115	  
116	  return {
117	    x: sum.x / cards.length,
118	    y: sum.y / cards.length
